property_summary: lockInGuess reverts exactly when the caller already has a pending guess (i.e., their stored block is nonzero).
A user who has not yet locked in a guess can always successfully call lockInGuess in the reference contract, but in the mutant such a call always reverts.

After any sequence of actions, if a user who already has a pending guess calls lockInGuess with valid payment, the reference contract reverts (block != 0) while the buggy contract allows the call to succeed and overwrite the guess.
In the reference contract, a user without a pending guess can lock in a guess; the buggy contract prevents this (reverts), so a fresh user’s lockInGuess call success flag differs.

In the reference contract, a user who has never called lockInGuess can successfully do so and the state is updated to reflect a pending guess; in the mutant, such a call always reverts, meaning no user can ever establish a pending guess.
In the reference contract, a user with a pending guess (guesses[user].block != 0) cannot call lockInGuess again, but the mutant incorrectly allows such a call to succeed and overwrite the guess.

After a successful lockInGuess, the lock block must be strictly greater than the current block number; the mutant can set it equal to the current block, causing the settle condition to be satisfied too early.

After a successful lockInGuess call, the recorded block number must be strictly greater than the current block number (block.number); the mutant sets it equal to block.number, violating this invariant.
